# Pathland Core Events

**Wire protocol version:** 1
**Status:** Draft
**Last Updated:** August 28, 2026

---

## Purpose

This document is the **catalog of core events** the Pathland protocol supports.
Events are the **raw inputs** a renderer reports about the user's interaction —
pointer motion, keys, value changes, text edits, scroll. Only the **core
events** are specified here; **gestures** (tap, long-press, drag, magnify,
rotate) are explicitly **out of scope** and are composed application-side from
the raw pointer events (see [Deferred: gestures](#deferred-gestures)).

- View catalog: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)
- Modifiers (properties): [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md)
- Wire format: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)

### Status legend

- **✅ Implemented** — the event command / listener bit exists in
  `pathland_core::constants` and is exercised today.
- **🚧 Draft** — the command / bit is **allocated in this document** (spec-first)
  but not implemented anywhere yet. IDs are reserved and MUST NOT be reused.

---

## Event model

Events flow **host → guest**. The renderer is the producer; the app/engine is
the consumer. Both directions of the protocol are binary and share the same
16-byte opcode format; events are `EVENT`-category (0x03) opcodes.

### Who emits what

- The **renderer** observes native input (a GTK controller, a DOM listener) and
  writes raw `EVENT` opcodes. It never interprets them into high-level actions.
- The **app** drains the events, composes gestures/handlers, and updates its
  bound `State` signals (which in turn re-emit `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`
  deltas).
- The renderer reports an event for a node **only if that node declared it**
  wants it, via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (`0x2005`, a u32
  bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type). This makes **any element**
  (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit events, not just controls.

### Target resolution

The renderer resolves `targetId` from its own rendered-output tree (its
`id → native element` map): the event's position is hit-tested against that
tree to find the deepest node with the matching listener bit. If no listener is
declared, the event is not reported.

### Transport paths

| Path | Mechanism |
|------|-----------|
| Shared memory (desktop/native) | The host writes `EVENT` opcodes into the event ring (host → guest) at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains at `eventReadCursor`. Events are consumed as written (no frame batching). |
| Network batch (SSR → browser) | Host → guest batches are the planned `0x0001` direction flag of the `PLPL` batch format; not yet implemented (see OPCODE.md Transport). |

### Encoding

Every event is a 16-byte opcode:

```
[Category=0x03][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
```

`TEXT_CHANGED` is the exception: its payload is an offset into the batch's
string section, so it is only fully decodable at the batch level (the same
convention as `STYLE::SET_TEXT`).

---

## Core event catalog

### Pointer

Pointer events carry a viewport-relative point in **logical points** (`B`=x,
`C`=y, f32).

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Status | SwiftUI counterpart |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|--------|---------------------|
| `POINTER_DOWN` | 0x01 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | ✅ | press (basis of `onTapGesture`, `Button` action) |
| `POINTER_MOVE` | 0x02 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `HOVER_ENTER` (0x0001) / `HOVER_LEAVE` (0x0002) | ✅ | hover/enter/leave, drag basis |
| `POINTER_UP` | 0x03 | targetId | x (f32) | y (f32) | `POINTER_SECONDARY` (0x0001) | ✅ | release (basis of `onTapGesture`) |

- **Flags**:
  - `POINTER_SECONDARY`: the secondary button (right mouse, long-press) rather
    than the primary.
  - `HOVER_ENTER` (bit 0 of `POINTER_MOVE`): the pointer just entered the
    node's bounds (is now hovering). `HOVER_LEAVE` (bit 1): the pointer just
    left. A plain move has neither bit set.
- **Listener bits**: `POINTER_DOWN` (bit 0), `POINTER_MOVE` (bit 1),
  `POINTER_UP` (bit 2).
- **Renderer**: attaches native press/hover recognition to the matching native
  element when the listener bit is set. Multiple pointer events may be reported
  for one physical gesture (down → several moves → up), all for the same
  `targetId` while the pointer stays over the node.

### Keyboard

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Status | SwiftUI counterpart |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|--------|---------------------|
| `KEY_DOWN` | 0x04 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | `KEY_REPEAT` (0x0002) | ✅ | `onKeyPress(.down)` |
| `KEY_UP` | 0x05 | targetId | keyCode (u16, low) | modifiers (u8, low) | — | ✅ | `onKeyPress(.up)` |

- **`keyCode`**: a **canonical, platform-independent logical key code** (a
  renderer maps native scancodes/key-codes onto this canonical set). The
  canonical set (letters/digits/arrows/Enter/Tab/…) is renderer-shared and
  documented in the conformance vectors.
- **`modifiers`**: u8 bitmask — `Shift`=0x01, `Control`=0x02, `Alt`=0x04,
  `Meta/Super`=0x08.
- **`KEY_REPEAT`**: bit 1 of flags; set when the key is an OS auto-repeat.
- **Listener bits**: `KEY_DOWN` (bit 3), `KEY_UP` (bit 4).
- **Focus**: keyboard events are reported to the focused node (the node that
  most recently gained focus), or to the node that declared the listener and
  has keyboard focus. See `FOCUS_CHANGED` below.

### Value

Value events carry a control's semantic value, resolved by the renderer from
its own native control geometry.

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Status | SwiftUI counterpart |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|--------|---------------------|
| `VALUE_CHANGED` | 0x06 | targetId | value (f32) | 0 | — | ✅ | `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Gauge`/`Picker`/`TabView` binding changes |

- **Semantics per control** (see [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) controls):
  - `SLIDER`/`STEPPER`/`GAUGE` — the numeric value in the control's range.
  - `SWITCH`/`CHECKBOX` — 0/1 (checked state; the same value the app writes to
    `SELECTED`).
  - `PICKER`/`MENU` — the selected option index.
  - `TAB_VIEW` — the active tab index.
  - `DATE_PICKER` — unix seconds (f32).
  - `COLOR_PICKER` — the packed `0xAARRGGBB` color reinterpreted as an f32 bit
    pattern.
- The app writes the received value into its bound `State`; the engine's
  signal flush re-emits the `SET_PROPERTY` delta back to the renderer (the
  renderer reflects its own native control).
- **No listener bit**: value-bearing controls are reported by the renderer by
  virtue of their component type, regardless of `EVENT_LISTENERS`. The
  renderer owns the gesture (e.g. slider drag) that produces them.

### Text

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Status | SwiftUI counterpart |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|--------|---------------------|
| `TEXT_CHANGED` | 0x07 | targetId | string offset | 0 | — | ✅ | `TextField` value binding |
| `FOCUS_CHANGED` | 0x08 | targetId | focused (0/1) | 0 | — | 🚧 | `@FocusState` |
| `EDITING_CHANGED` | 0x09 | targetId | editing (0/1) | 0 | — | 🚧 | `TextField`/`Slider` `onEditingChanged` |
| `SUBMIT` | 0x0A | targetId | 0 | 0 | — | 🚧 | `TextField` `onSubmit` / `onCommit` |

- **`TEXT_CHANGED`**: the new text is a length-prefixed entry
  (`[u32 byteLength][bytes…]`) in the **batch's string section**, referenced by
  the *relative* offset in `B` — exactly the convention of `STYLE::SET_TEXT`.
  A bare opcode cannot resolve the text; batch-aware decoders
  (`pathland-core-transport`, Java `FrameCodec`, TS `decoder.ts`) must resolve
  it. The event is reported on **every** edit, including intermediate edits,
  not only on commit.
- **`FOCUS_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 gained focus, 0 lost focus. The renderer reports
  it for nodes that declared the `FOCUS` listener bit (bit 5). Focus is what
  routes subsequent `KEY_*` events.
- **`EDITING_CHANGED`**: `B` = 1 editing session began, 0 ended. Reported for
  nodes that declared the `EDITING` listener bit (bit 6).
- **`SUBMIT`**: the user committed the field (Enter). Reported for nodes that
  declared the `SUBMIT` listener bit (bit 7). `B` MAY carry the current text as
  a string-section offset (reserved for future use; 0 today).

### Scroll

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Status | SwiftUI counterpart |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|--------|---------------------|
| `SCROLL` | 0x0B | targetId | offsetX (f32) | offsetY (f32) | — | 🚧 | `ScrollView` offset, `onScrollPhaseChange` |
| `WHEEL` | 0x0C | targetId | deltaX (f32) | deltaY (f32) | — | 🚧 | `onScrollWheelEvent` / trackpad |

- **`SCROLL`**: the content offset of a `SCROLLVIEW` (logical points), reported
  for nodes that declared the `SCROLL` listener bit (bit 8). The renderer
  reports the absolute offset after each scroll delta.
- **`WHEEL`**: raw wheel/trackpad deltas (logical points), reported for nodes
  that declared the `WHEEL` listener bit (bit 9). Renderers map native scroll
  deltas (GTK `GtkEventControllerScroll`, DOM `wheel`) onto x/y deltas.

---

## Event listeners (`EVENT_LISTENERS`)

`EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) is a u32 bitmask set via `SET_PROPERTY` (U32). Each
bit requests one raw-input event kind for the node:

| Bit | Mask | Event | Status |
|-----|------|-------|--------|
| 0 | `0x00000001` | `POINTER_DOWN` | ✅ |
| 1 | `0x00000002` | `POINTER_MOVE` (incl. hover enter/leave) | ✅ |
| 2 | `0x00000004` | `POINTER_UP` | ✅ |
| 3 | `0x00000008` | `KEY_DOWN` | ✅ |
| 4 | `0x00000010` | `KEY_UP` | ✅ |
| 5 | `0x00000020` | `FOCUS_CHANGED` | 🚧 |
| 6 | `0x00000040` | `EDITING_CHANGED` | 🚧 |
| 7 | `0x00000080` | `SUBMIT` | 🚧 |
| 8 | `0x00000100` | `SCROLL` | 🚧 |
| 9 | `0x00000200` | `WHEEL` | 🚧 |
| 10–31 | — | reserved | — |

Convenience aliases (DSL-side): `POINTER = bits 0|1|2`.

DSL surfaces:

- Rust: `pathland_view::pointer_events(mask)` modifier + `listener::*` bits;
  `on_tap_gesture` sets `POINTER_DOWN | POINTER_UP`.
- Java: `TapGestureView` / `EVENT_LISTENERS` via the emitter; host forwards raw
  `EVENT` batches into bound `State` signals.

---

## Deferred: gestures

SwiftUI gestures — `onTapGesture`, `onLongPressGesture`, `DragGesture`,
`MagnifyGesture`, `RotateGesture` — are **not protocol events**. Per the
protocol's raw-inputs-only rule, they are **composed application-side** from
the raw `POINTER_*` / `KEY_*` events above:

- **Tap** = `POINTER_DOWN` then `POINTER_UP` on the same `targetId` within the
  platform's tap window (implemented today as `TapRecognizer` /
  `on_tap_gesture`).
- **Long-press** = `POINTER_DOWN` held past a threshold.
- **Drag** = `POINTER_DOWN` + `POINTER_MOVE` sequence.
- **Magnify / rotate** = multi-pointer deltas; the underlying raw events are
  `POINTER_*` (multi-touch reported per pointer).

A future "gesture recognition" layer MAY define app-side recognizers, but the
wire protocol will never carry interpreted gestures — only raw inputs.

---

## Reserved event command IDs

| Range | Use |
|-------|-----|
| `0x01`–`0x07` | Implemented core events (this file) |
| `0x08`–`0x0C` | Draft core events (this file) |
| `0x0D`–`0x3F` | Future core events (unallocated) |
| `0x40`–`0xFF` | Custom/application events |

A renderer/decoder MUST skip unknown event commands and continue.

---

## Conformance

Event encode/decode round-trips and golden byte vectors (incl. raw-input
`EVENT` and network-batch bytes) live in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md).
New events added here MUST add vectors before implementation.

1: # Pathland Core Events
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** August 28, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Purpose
10: 
11: This document is the **catalog of core events** the Pathland protocol supports.
12: Events are the **raw inputs** a renderer reports about the user's interaction —
13: pointer motion, keys, value changes, text edits, scroll. Only the **core
14: events** are specified here; **gestures** (tap, long-press, drag, magnify,
15: rotate) are explicitly **out of scope** and are composed application-side from
16: the raw pointer events (see [Deferred: gestures](#deferred-gestures)).
17: 
18: - View catalog: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)
19: - Modifiers (properties): [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md)
20: - Wire format: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
21: 
22: ### Status legend
23: 
24: - **✅ Implemented** — the event command / listener bit exists in
25:   `pathland_core::constants` and is exercised today.
26: - **🚧 Draft** — the command / bit is **allocated in this document** (spec-first)
27:   but not implemented anywhere yet. IDs are reserved and MUST NOT be reused.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## Event model
32: 
33: Events flow **host → guest**. The renderer is the producer; the app/engine is
34: the consumer. Both directions of the protocol are binary and share the same
35: 16-byte opcode format; events are `EVENT`-category (0x03) opcodes.
36: 
37: ### Who emits what
38: 
39: - The **renderer** observes native input (a GTK controller, a DOM listener) and
40:   writes raw `EVENT` opcodes. It never interprets them into high-level actions.
41: - The **app** drains the events, composes gestures/handlers, and updates its
42:   bound `State` signals (which in turn re-emit `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`
43:   deltas).
44: - The renderer reports an event for a node **only if that node declared it**
45:   wants it, via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (`0x2005`, a u32
46:   bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type). This makes **any element**
47:   (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit events, not just controls.

1: # Pathland Conformance Test Vectors
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Encoding:** little-endian
5: **Opcode size:** 16 bytes
6: 
7: This document provides **golden byte arrays** for the Pathland opcode protocol (see [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)). A conforming implementation MUST:
8: 
9: - encode each opcode to exactly these 16 bytes, and
10: - decode these bytes to the equivalent opcode.
11: 
12: The vectors are enforced by the reference Rust encoder (`pathland-core`,
13: `crates/pathland-core/src/conformance.rs`).
14: 
15: ## Opcode Layout
16: 
17: ```
18: [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
19: ```
20: 
21: All multi-byte fields little-endian. `A`/`B`/`C` may carry `f32` bit patterns.
22: 
23: ## Vectors
24: 
25: ### 1. TREE:CREATE_NODE (id=1, VSTACK=0x0002)
26: 
27: ```
28: 01 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
29: ```
30: 
31: - `01` category = TREE
32: - `01` command = CREATE_NODE
33: - `00 00` flags = 0
34: - `01 00 00 00` A = nodeId = 1
35: - `02 00 00 00` B = componentType = 0x0002 (VSTACK)
36: - `00 00 00 00` C = 0
37: 
38: ### 2. TREE:INSERT_CHILD (parent=0, child=1, index=APPEND)
39: 
40: ```
41: 01 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 FF FF FF FF
42: ```
43: 
44: - `01` category = TREE
45: - `03` command = INSERT_CHILD
46: - `00 00` flags = 0
47: - `00 00 00 00` A = parentId = 0
48: - `01 00 00 00` B = childId = 1
49: - `FF FF FF FF` C = APPEND (`u32::MAX`)
50: 
51: ### 3. TREE:MOVE_CHILD (parent=1, child=2, newIndex=0)
52: 
53: ```
54: 01 05 00 00 01 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
55: ```
56: 
57: - `01` category = TREE
58: - `05` command = MOVE_CHILD
59: - `00 00` flags = 0
60: - `01 00 00 00` A = parentId = 1
61: - `02 00 00 00` B = childId = 2
62: - `00 00 00 00` C = newIndex = 0
63: 
64: ### 4. STYLE:SET_PROPERTY (id=1, propertyId=SPACING=0x0001, valueType=F32, 4.0)
65: 
66: ```
67: 02 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 01 00 04 00 00 00 80 40
68: ```
69: 
70: - `02` category = STYLE
71: - `01` command = SET_PROPERTY
72: - `00 00` flags = 0
73: - `01 00 00 00` A = nodeId = 1
74: - `01 00 04 00` B = `(valueType << 16) | propertyId` = `(0x04 << 16) | 0x0001`
75:   - low two bytes `01 00` = propertyId = 0x0001 (SPACING)
76:   - high byte `04` = valueType = 0x04 (F32)
77: - `00 00 80 40` C = 4.0 (f32 LE: 0x40800000)
78: 
79: ### 5. STYLE:SET_PROPERTY (id=1, propertyId=COLOR=0x100A, valueType=COLOR=0x07, rgba=0xFF0000FF)

81: ```

83: ```
84: 
85: - `02` category = STYLE
86: - `01` command = SET_PROPERTY
87: - `00 00` flags = 0
88: - `01 00 00 00` A = nodeId = 1
89: - `0A 10 07 00` B = `(valueType << 16) | propertyId` = `(0x07 << 16) | 0x100A`
90:   - low two bytes `0A 10` = propertyId = 0x100A (COLOR)
91:   - high byte `07` = valueType = 0x07 (COLOR)
92: - `FF 00 00 FF` C = 0xFF0000FF (opaque blue, `0xAARRGGBB`)
93: 
94: ### 6. STYLE:SET_TEXT (id=1, arenaRef=0)
95: 
96: ```
97: 02 03 00 00 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
98: ```
99: 
100: - `02` category = STYLE
101: - `03` command = SET_TEXT
102: - `00 00` flags = 0
103: - `01 00 00 00` A = nodeId = 1
104: - `00 00 00 00` B = arenaRef = 0 (entry is `[u32 length][bytes]` in the arena)
105: - `00 00 00 00` C = 0
106:

111: ```

114: - `01` command = RESET
115: - `00 00` flags = 0
116: - `00 00 00 00` A = 0
117: - `00 00 00 00` B = 0
118: - `00 00 00 00` C = 0

124: ```

126: - `03` category = EVENT
127: - `01` command = POINTER_DOWN
128: - `00 00` flags = 0
129: - `05 00 00 00` A = targetId = 5
130: - `00 00 20 41` B = 10.0 (f32 LE: 0x41200000)

137: ```

142: - `05 00 00 00` A = targetId = 5

144: - `00 00 A0 41` C = 20.0 (f32 LE: 0x41A00000)

150: ```

157: - `00 00 A0 41` C = 20.0 (f32 LE: 0x41A00000)
158: 
159: ### 11. EVENT:KEY_DOWN (target=5, keyCode='A'=0x41, modifiers=0x01, repeat)
160: 
161: ```
162: 03 04 02 00 05 00 00 00 41 00 00 00 01 00 00 00
163: ```
164: 
165: - `03` category = EVENT
166: - `04` command = KEY_DOWN
167: - `02 00` flags = 0x0002 (`KEY_REPEAT`)
168: - `05 00 00 00` A = targetId = 5
169: - `41 00 00 00` B = keyCode = 0x41 (`'A'`, low u16)
170: - `01 00 00 00` C = modifiers = 0x01 (low u8)
171: 
172: ### 12. EVENT:KEY_UP (target=5, keyCode='A'=0x41, modifiers=0x01)
173: 
174: ```
175: 03 05 00 00 05 00 00 00 41 00 00 00 01 00 00 00
176: ```
177: 
178: - `03` category = EVENT
179: - `05` command = KEY_UP
180: - `00 00` flags = 0
181: - `05 00 00 00` A = targetId = 5
182: - `41 00 00 00` B = keyCode = 0x41 (`'A'`, low u16)
183: - `01 00 00 00` C = modifiers = 0x01 (low u8)
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## Directions
188: 
189: - `TREE` / `STYLE` are **guest → host** (application → renderer).
190: - `EVENT` is **host → guest** (renderer → application): raw pointer/keyboard
191:   inputs with a host-resolved `targetId`. A conforming EVENT encoder/decoder
192:   MUST reproduce vectors 8–12 exactly.
193: - `META` is both directions.
194: 
195: ## Frame Conformance
196: 
197: A complete frame is: delta opcodes written into consecutive ring slots, then a
198: `frameCount` increment in the header block. Ring slot `i` occupies bytes
199: `[ringOffset + i*16, ringOffset + i*16 + 16)`.
200: 
201: The header block layout and ring semantics are defined in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#linear-memory-layout).
202: 
203: The host → guest event ring shares the same 16-byte slot format and lives at
204: `eventRingOffset` (header `0x2A`), with `eventReadCursor` (0x36, guest-owned)
205: and `eventWriteCursor` (0x3A, host-owned). A host writing `EVENT:POINTER_UP`
206: into the event ring must reproduce the exact vector-11 bytes in the slot at
207: `eventWriteCursor`, then advance `eventWriteCursor`; the guest advances
208: `eventReadCursor` after draining.
209: 
210: ## Network Batch Conformance
211: 
212: A network batch serializes opcodes + an arena delta (see
213: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#transport)). A conforming batch encoder/decoder MUST
214: reproduce the following bytes exactly.
215: 
216: ### 13. NETWORK:BATCH (frameCount=1, one CREATE_NODE, arena delta = "Hi")
217: 
218: The single opcode is `TREE:CREATE_NODE (id=1, VSTACK)` from vector 1. The arena
219: delta is the self-describing entry for `"Hi"`: `[02 00 00 00][48 69]`.
220: 
221: ```
222: 4C 50 4C 50 01 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 01 00 00 00
223: 01 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
224: 06 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 48 69
225: ```
226: 
227: - `4C 50 4C 50` = magic `PLPL` (u32 `0x504C504C`, little-endian)
228: - `01 00` = version 1
229: - `00 00` = flags (guest → host)
230: - `01 00 00 00` = frameCount = 1
231: - `01 00 00 00` = opcodeCount = 1
232: - `01 01 00 00 01 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` = the CREATE_NODE opcode (16 bytes)
233: - `06 00 00 00` = arenaDeltaLen = 6
234: - `02 00 00 00 48 69` = arena entry `[len=2]["Hi"]`
235: 
236: ### 14. NETWORK:BATCH (frameCount=2, empty opcode list, empty arena delta)
237: 
238: ```
239: 4C 50 4C 50 01 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
240: 00 00 00 00
241: ```

245: - `00 00` = flags
246: - `02 00 00 00` = frameCount = 2
247: - `00 00 00 00` = opcodeCount = 0
248: - `00 00 00 00` = arenaDeltaLen = 0

content.text:
## Consistency review

The three files are **internally consistent with each other and with OPCODE.md/CONFORMANCE.md** for everything already implemented. All draft IDs fall in reserved/free ranges with no collisions, and the OPCODE.md pointers are in place. But a full cross-check surfaces several gaps — some **new** (introduced by the drafts) and some **pre-existing** (now made visible by the new files).

### Real gaps that would block an AI implementer

1. **`Picker`/`Menu`/`TabView` options have no wire encoding.** PRIMITIVES says options are "STRING entries" / "same option encoding as Picker", but the protocol has no list/array value type or multi-option mechanism. A renderer cannot be written from the docs. Fix: options = **child nodes** (consistent with the retained tree, like `List` rows), or add a `STRING_LIST` arena value type. I recommend child nodes.

2. **Date precision is wrong.** `DATE_VALUE`/`VALUE_CHANGED` as **f32 unix seconds** can't be second-accurate: at ~2×10⁹ (today), an f32 ulp ≈ 128 s. Fix: `DATE_VALUE` = **U32** unix seconds (covers 1970–2106) and document that the event carries the u32 bit pattern for the app to reinterpret.

3. **`GROUP` modifier propagation is underspecified.** The flat protocol has no property inheritance; "Group applies modifiers to all children" needs a defined mechanism. Fix: document `GROUP` as an **emitter-side construct** (app copies modifiers onto each child; no `GROUP` node on the wire), which also lets the renderer hoist trivially.

4. **`value_type` mismatch: docs say ENUM/U32, implementations emit F32.** OPCODE.md + the three files say `ALIGNMENT`/`TEXT_ALIGNMENT`/`TRUNCATION_MODE` are `ENUM`, `LINE_LIMIT` is `U32`, `FONT_FAMILY` is `STRING` — but `constants.rs value_type_for` and both DSLs emit `F32` for all of these (Java's `forProperty` fixes only `FONT_FAMILY`→STRING; Rust emits `value_type::F32` for ALIGNMENT in its own renderer tests). A decoder written from the docs would diverge from the Rust/Java engines. Pre-existing, now prominent. Fix: update `value_type_for`/`forProperty` to match the docs (spec wins).

### Smaller gaps / tidy-ups

5. **Enum value tables are scattered** — ALIGNMENT, TEXT_ALIGNMENT, TRUNCATION_MODE, FONT_WEIGHT scale, FONT_STYLE/DESIGN, TEXT_CASE, CONTENT_MODE, CONTROL_SIZE, DATE_PICKER_MODE, PICKER_STYLE, SHAPE_KIND, ROLE, STATE are split across PRIMITIVES/MODIFIERS, some defined in only one place. Recommend one authoritative consolidated enum table (appendix in MODIFIERS.md) so implementers have a single source.
6. **OPCODE.md property tables stay partial** — the constraint table omits `CONTENT_MARGINS` (0x0005); the text properties (`TEXT`, `LINE_LIMIT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`) appear in no OPCODE.md table; the `EVENT_LISTENERS` table stops at bit 4. The three files fill these, but OPCODE.md is the "primary" spec — fold pointers in.
7. **Pre-existing append dual-encoding:** OPCODE.md says `INSERT_CHILD` append = flags `0x0001`, but CONFORMANCE vector 2 and `constants.rs` use `C = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`). Reconcile which is canonical.
8. **No pointers from `CONFORMANCE.md` or `AGENTS.md`** to the three new files — AGENTS.md is the first doc an AI reads and its component/property tables now partially duplicate the new catalogs.

### Proposed fix plan (spec + minimal code, spec-first)

- **PRIMITIVES.md**: define Picker/Menu/TabView options as child nodes; change `DATE_VALUE` to U32 unix seconds; document `GROUP` as emitter-side.

Good questions. Here's the answer on dates, then the plan.

## Java's `Instant` and cross-language date standards

There is a de facto numeric standard: **Unix/POSIX epoch seconds** — seconds since `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` as a **signed integer**. Java's `Instant` is literally that (i64 seconds) + nanoseconds. Rust (`SystemTime`/`chrono`), C `time_t`, Go `time.Unix()`, and Python all use the same epoch.

The catch for our protocol: pre-1970 dates need **negative seconds**, and the practical range is a **64-bit** quantity. With 32-bit payloads:
- `I32` seconds → only **1902–2038** (not "way before 1970").
- `U32` seconds → 1970–2106 (nothing before 1970).

The cross-language standard that *does* cover arbitrary ranges (including far before 1970) with second precision is the **ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 string** (e.g. `1890-06-15T00:00:00Z`) — every language parses it into its native datetime (Java `Instant.parse`, Rust `chrono`, JS `Date`, Python). It also fits the protocol's existing `STRING` value type + arena with zero protocol extension.

So: numeric-epoch-seconds is "Instant-like" but needs 64 bits we don't have; ISO 8601 string is the universal range-unlimited standard that fits our wire.

1. **Date**: `DATE_VALUE` (0x2011) → `STRING`, RFC 3339 UTC. Value changes reported by a new draft event `DATE_CHANGED` (0x0D, `A=targetId, B=string offset`, mirroring `TEXT_CHANGED` — no listener bit, like other value controls). Removes the f32-precision problem entirely.
2. **`Group`**: remove from PRIMITIVES.md — drop the Layout table row, the section, the `0x0011` draft allocation (0x0011 becomes unallocated/reserved, never reused). No other file references it.

## Date encoding: three u32 fields

| Field | Opcode slot | Type | Range |
|-------|-------------|------|-------|
| **days since epoch** | `B` | `I32` (bit pattern) | ±2.1×10⁹ days ≈ **±5.9 million years** — pre-1970 is negative days, no limit in practice |
| **second of day** | `C` | `U32` | 0..86,399 |
| **nanos of second** | (see below) | `I32` | 0..999,999,999 |

The math: a targeted opcode always spends `A` on node/target id, leaving 64 bits. `days` (32) + `second-of-day` (17 bits) = 49 bits fits exactly; adding `nanos` (30 bits) needs 79 bits — it **does not fit inline**. Every language can split an Instant into (days-since-epoch, second-of-day, nanos) with its stdlib, so this stays "the Instant standard" you wanted.

Good instinct, but one arithmetic check: **nanos-of-day doesn't fit a u32**.

- nanos-of-day max = 86,400 × 10⁹ = **86.4×10¹²** ≈ 2^46.4 → needs **47 bits**
- days (I32, 32 bits) + nanos-of-day (47 bits) = **79 bits** > the 64 free bits in `B`+`C` (and u32 alone caps at 4.29×10⁹ ≈ 4.3 seconds of nanos)

So "days + nanos of day" can't be two 32-bit fields. What *does* fit in two u32 fields:

| Encoding | Precision | Bits | Range |
|----------|-----------|------|-------|
| days (I32) + **millis of day** (U32) | **millisecond** | 32+27=59 | ±5.9M years ✅ |
| days (I32) + second of day (U32) | second | 32+17=49 | ±5.9M years ✅ |

millis-of-day = `0..86,400,000` (2^27), every language computes it from its epoch instant (`epochMilli % 86_400_000`). Nanosecond fidelity simply cannot fit two fields — if you need it, it's the three-field split (days + second-of-day inline, optional `DATE_NANOS` companion property, default 0).

Check the numbers again — **nanos-of-hour doesn't fit either**.

- nanos-of-hour max = 3,600 × 10⁹ = **3.6×10¹²** ≈ 2^41.7 → needs **42 bits** (u32 caps at 4.29×10⁹ ≈ 4.3 seconds of nanos)
- Any "nanos-of-<unit≥1min>" needs ≥36 bits, and with a coarse field always exceeds the 64 free bits in `B`+`C`.

Here's the full fit table for a two-field pair (coarse = I32, fine = U32):

| Coarse (I32) | Fine (U32) | Precision | Range | Fits 64 bits? |
|--------------|------------|-----------|-------|---------------|
| days | millis-of-day | ms | ±5.9M yr | ✅ (59) |
| hours | millis-of-hour | ms | ±245k yr | ✅ (54) |
| **hours** | **micros-of-hour** | **μs** | **±245k yr** | **✅ (64, exact)** |
| days | micros-of-day | μs | ±5.9M yr | ❌ (69) |
| any | nanos-of-* | ns | — | ❌ |

The **maximum precision two u32 fields can express** is `hours since epoch` (I32) + `micros of hour` (U32, 0..3,600,000,000) — exactly 64 bits, microsecond precision, ±245k years from 1970 (so pre-1970 by centuries is trivial). Nanosecond fidelity is only reachable via the three-value split (days + second-of-day inline + optional `DATE_NANOS` companion property).

247: Events are the **raw inputs**: the renderer reports what happened (a pointer
248: went down/moved/up, a key went down/up) and resolves which node it hit via its
249: own rendered-output tree. High-level interpretations — tap, drag, long-press —
250: are built by the guest/app from these raw inputs and are **not** part of the
251: protocol.
252: 
253: #### Event listeners (which nodes emit events)
254: 
255: A renderer reports raw events only for nodes that declared they want them. The
256: application declares this intent through the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic
257: property (`0x2005`, a u32 bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type).
258: Each bit requests a raw-input event kind (see [`listener`] flags):
259:

264: | 2 | `0x00000004` | `POINTER_UP` | Report pointer-up for this node |
265: | 3 | `0x00000008` | `KEY_DOWN` | Report key-down |
266: | 4 | `0x00000010` | `KEY_UP` | Report key-up |

## Consistency review after the latest changes

**Good news — the three files now agree with each other and with OPCODE.md/CONFORMANCE.md on everything recent:**
- `SET_DATE` (0x04) ↔ `DATE_CHANGED` (0x0D) use the same `days (I32) + millis-of-day (U32)` shape across OPCODE/PRIMITIVES/EVENTS.
- `Group` is fully gone (`0x0011` marked unallocated/reserved, no stale references).
- Enum values in the new MODIFIERS appendix match PRIMITIVES (ALIGNMENT, SHAPE_KIND, CONTENT_MODE, DATE_PICKER_MODE, PICKER_STYLE, …).
- Append reconciliation holds: OPCODE.md now says `C = u32::MAX`, which matches CONFORMANCE vector 2 and `constants.rs::APPEND`.
- `CONTENT_MARGINS` + text properties added to OPCODE.md; listener-bit note covers bits 5–9; pointers in CONFORMANCE/AGENTS all resolve.

**Remaining gaps (ranked):**

1. **`ROLE`/`STATE` value sets claimed but undefined.** MODIFIERS.md §5 and the appendix say their enumerated values are "defined in OPCODE.md" — but OPCODE.md lists them only as `ENUM` with **no values**. They're also marked ✅ implemented, so an implementer has nothing to code against. Fix: define the value sets in OPCODE.md (recommended) or reword the appendix to "not yet defined; renderer-shared, future work". (Small, spec-only.)

2. **`value_type` spec↔code mismatch — deferred, still open (top implementation follow-up).** The docs say `ALIGNMENT`/`TEXT_ALIGNMENT`/`TRUNCATION_MODE` → `ENUM`, `LINE_LIMIT` → `U32`, `FONT_FAMILY` → `STRING`, but `constants.rs value_type_for` (and the Rust DSL/GTK renderer) emit `F32` for all of these; Java's `forProperty` fixes only `FONT_FAMILY`. A renderer written strictly from the docs would emit different value-type bytes than the reference engine. No conformance-vector conflict yet (vectors don't cover them), but it will bite at implementation time.

3. **`DATE_CHANGED` "works over a network batch" is slightly ahead.** Host→guest network batches (batch flag `0x0001`) are still unimplemented per OPCODE.md Transport; the encoding is inline so the claim is valid once that direction lands — just flagging the wording.

4. **`constants.rs` still documents the deprecated `INSERT_APPEND` flag (0x0001).** Spec now canonicalizes `APPEND` (u32::MAX); the code comment (`constants.rs:80-81`) and the `flag::INSERT_APPEND` constant describe the old flag. No wire conflict (engine emits explicit indices; vector 2 uses the sentinel), but comment + spec should agree when the code is next touched.

5. **Minor: signed-field convention.** OPCODE.md payload conventions don't explicitly say `B`/`C` can carry signed (I32) bit patterns for dedicated commands like `SET_DATE` — one clarifying line would help implementers.

### Proposed follow-up (spec-only, if you want it)
Fix item 1 (define `ROLE`/`STATE` value sets in OPCODE.md, or reword the appendix) and add item 5's one-line clarification. Items 2–4 are implementation/code-comment work — I'd defer them until you want the `value_type` alignment (the earlier "Spec + value_type alignment" scope).

69: ### Payload encoding conventions
70: 
71: - **Float payloads** (`spacing`, `padding`, sizes) are stored as raw `f32` (IEEE 754) bit patterns in a `u32` field.
72: - **Node IDs** are `u32`.
73: - **Component types / property IDs** are `u16`; when packed into a 4-byte payload they occupy the low two bytes (the high bytes are reserved / zero unless documented).
74: - **Arena references** are a `u32` byte offset into the arena region (see [Arena](#arena)).
75: - **Colors** are packed `0xAARRGGBB` in sRGB (see [Colors](#colors)).

79: - `Category == 0` is reserved (invalid).
80: - `Command == 0` in any category is reserved (invalid).
81: - `Category 0x80-0xFF`: custom/extended categories.

input.newString:
### Payload encoding conventions

- **Float payloads** (`spacing`, `padding`, sizes) are stored as raw `f32` (IEEE 754) bit patterns in a `u32` field.
- **Signed payloads** (the `I32` value type, and dedicated commands like `SET_DATE`'s days-since-epoch) are stored as the raw two's-complement bit pattern of a signed value in a `u32` field; a consumer reinterprets the field as `i32`.
- **Node IDs** are `u32`.
- **Component types / property IDs** are `u16`; when packed into a 4-byte payload they occupy the low two bytes (the high bytes are reserved / zero unless documented).
- **Arena references** are a `u32` byte offset into the arena region (see [Arena](#arena)).
- **Colors** are packed `0xAARRGGBB` in sRGB (see [Colors](#colors)).

## Consistency review — final state

**The docs are now internally consistent.** Cross-checked across PRIMITIVES/MODIFIERS/EVENTS and OPCODE/CONFORMANCE/AGENTS:

- `SET_DATE` (0x04) ↔ `DATE_CHANGED` (0x0D) share the `days (I32) + millis-of-day (U32)` shape everywhere.
- `Group` gone; `0x0011` marked unallocated/reserved. `DATE_VALUE` gone; `0x2011` marked unallocated.
- `Picker`/`Menu` options = child nodes; enum appendix values match PRIMITIVES; `ROLE`/`STATE` value sets now defined in OPCODE.md and correctly referenced from MODIFIERS (no more "defined elsewhere" claim).
- Append canonicalized to `C = u32::MAX` (matches CONFORMANCE vector 2 + `constants.rs::APPEND`); no stale `0x0001`-append text anywhere.
- `CONTENT_MARGINS` + text properties present; listener bits 5–9 pointed at EVENTS.md; signed-field (I32) convention added; all cross-file anchors resolve.

**Remaining gaps (all pre-existing/deferred implementation work, not doc conflicts):**

1. **`value_type` spec↔code mismatch — the only substantive one left.** The docs are canonical: `ALIGNMENT`/`TEXT_ALIGNMENT`/`TRUNCATION_MODE` → `ENUM`, `LINE_LIMIT` → `U32`, `FONT_FAMILY` → `STRING`. But `constants.rs value_type_for` and the Rust DSL/GTK renderer emit `F32` for all five (Java's `forProperty` fixes only `FONT_FAMILY`). The `FONT_FAMILY` deviation is flagged in MODIFIERS §2, but the ENUM/U32 ones aren't, and MODIFIERS still says the table "mirrors `value_type_for`" (line 286) — now misleading.
   - Spec-only now: reword "mirrors `value_type_for`" + add a deviation note for the ENUM/U32 properties (mirroring the FONT_FAMILY note).

2. **`constants.rs` still documents the deprecated `INSERT_APPEND` flag (0x0001)** (`flag::INSERT_APPEND` + comment). No wire conflict — comment cleanup when code is touched.
3. **Minor wording:** EVENTS.md `DATE_CHANGED` says it "works over a network batch", but the host→guest batch direction isn't implemented yet — it will be true when that lands.

Good question — and the deeper check it prompted changes one earlier recommendation. Here's the full picture.

## 1. How SwiftUI transmits font family

SwiftUI passes the concrete family as a **String** — the font family / postscript name — via `.font(.custom("Georgia", size: 18))`. Generic families are **enums** (`.fontDesign(.serif/.rounded/.monospaced)`), resolved to the platform's native font by the renderer. CSS (`font-family: "Georgia"`) and GTK (`PangoFontDescription` family) are also string-named. So `FONT_FAMILY` = **STRING** is correct; SwiftUI never transmits a numeric font ID.

## New finding: the ENUM-vs-F32 claim was backwards

I verified the actual wire usage across the whole stack: the Rust DSL, Java DSL, **GTK, HTML, and Angular ngui renderers all read `ALIGNMENT` (and `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`) as `f32`** (`f32::from_bits`). The spec's "ENUM, low byte of `C`" doesn't match any implementation. So the right fix is **spec → F32-carried numeric enum codes** (the enum value as an f32 bit pattern), not a renderer migration. That's a doc-only change and makes everything consistent with zero risk. `value_type::ENUM` stays available for explicitly-ENUM-coded properties.

Also confirmed: `host.rs:61-71` **ignores the `INSERT_CHILD` index entirely** (appends by push), and `MOVE_CHILD` honors the `APPEND` sentinel (`usize::MAX`). So `flag::INSERT_APPEND` is read by **nothing** — removing it is safe.

## Plan

**A. Spec (docs):**
1. **OPCODE.md** — value-type conventions: enum-valued properties are carried as F32 numeric codes; update `ALIGNMENT`, `ROLE`/`STATE`, and the text-props table accordingly.
2. **MODIFIERS.md** — fix "mirrors `value_type_for`" wording; `ALIGNMENT`/`TEXT_ALIGNMENT`/`TRUNCATION_MODE` → F32 (numeric code); enum-appendix intro says codes are carried as F32; keep `LINE_LIMIT`→U32, `FONT_FAMILY`→STRING.
3. **PRIMITIVES.md** — align `ALIGNMENT` mentions.
4. **EVENTS.md** — tighten `DATE_CHANGED` "works over a network batch" (host→guest batches not implemented yet).

**B. Code (safe, dormant paths):**
5. `constants.rs value_type_for`: `FONT_FAMILY` → `STRING`, `LINE_LIMIT` → `U32` (Java `ValueTypes.forProperty` add `LINE_LIMIT` → U32; `FONT_FAMILY` already STRING).
6. `INSERT_APPEND` cleanup: remove `flag::INSERT_APPEND` + stale doc comments in `constants.rs`, remove `Commands.Flags.INSERT_APPEND` in Java, and pass `flags=0` in `RingOpcodeSink`/`FrameOpcodeSink.insertChild` (keep `index=-1` = APPEND sentinel). No reader/renderer references it.

No conformance-vector changes needed (vector 2 already uses flags `00 00`).

Confirm and I'll implement A + B on `docs/primitive-specs` (spec edits + the small Rust/Java cleanups).

The protocol primitives are `SWITCH` (0x0006) and `CHECKBOX` (0x000D); I'd listed `Toggle` as a row/section alias for both, which contradicts the file's own purpose ("primitive views the protocol must support"). There's no technical reason for it — it was just to surface the SwiftUI↔protocol mapping, which belongs as a note under the real primitives, not as a primitive row.

Note: the Angular ngui renderer already treats them as distinct (`SWITCH` → `ui-toggle`, `CHECKBOX` → `ui-checkbox`), and `EVENTS.md`/`OPCODE.md` reference `SWITCH`/`CHECKBOX` directly — only PRIMITIVES.md conflates them.

### Plan (PRIMITIVES.md only)

1. **Controls & Indicators table** — replace the `Toggle` row with two rows:
   - `Switch` → `SWITCH` 0x0006, ✅, SELECTED, `VALUE_CHANGED` (0/1)

### Consistency question
`Link` (→ `BUTTON`) and `AsyncImage` (→ `IMAGE`) are the same pattern — listed as rows but clearly marked as mappings (`(→ ...)`), so they don't claim to be primitives. Want me to also normalize those two into mapping notes under `BUTTON`/`IMAGE` (removing their rows), or leave them as-is?

Also fine to leave `ROLE` value `8 = Switch/Toggle` in OPCODE.md — that's a role enum, not a primitive.

### Key Architectural Rules & Guidelines to Document

#### 1. Core Structural Classification: Primitives vs. Semantic Controls
Explicitly divide all supported nodes into two fundamental structural categories:

*   **Primitive Drawing Nodes (`0x01`–`0x0F`):** Low-level, non-decomposable building blocks (`Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape`, `Spacer`, `Divider`).
    *   *Behavior:* The server dictates exact visual content and structural properties. The client platform renderer measures layout geometry, handles font/image assets, and paints pixels directly onto the canvas or native layout tree. They do not hold independent interaction state machines.
*   **Semantic Control Nodes (`0x20`–`0x2F`):** High-order interaction and input controls (`Button`, `TextField`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `Picker`).
    *   *Behavior:* Encapsulate intent, two-way bindings (`PROP_BINDING_ID`), accessibility traits, and local interaction physics (e.g., 120 FPS client-side thumb dragging).

---

#### 2. Dual-Mode Rendering Pipeline & Platform Delegation
Document the universal rendering rules for Semantic Controls:

*   **Native Token Mode (Leaf Control):** When a semantic control node has no child layout tree (`childrenIds` is empty), the client platform MUST delegate rendering entirely to its native OS control (`UISlider`/`NSSlider`, `GtkScale`, `GtkCheckButton`, `<ui-slider>`).
    *   System style modifiers (e.g., `PROP_TOGGLE_STYLE = CHECKBOX`) act as visual style tokens—they force the platform to switch native control variants without emitting child nodes over the wire.
*   **Composite Override Mode (Container Control):** When a semantic control contains child nodes (or when a custom style body is defined on the server), the client platform MUST suppress its default native control visuals, render the custom view tree sent by the server, and wrap that layout tree with native touch/click gestures, focus states, and event handlers.
*   **Leaf Property Fallbacks:** If a control (such as `Button` `0x20`) arrives with an empty `childrenIds` list, client renderers MUST check for direct string properties (e.g., `PROP_TEXT` `0x0001`) before falling back to rendering an empty platform control shell.

---

#### 3. Transport-Aware Event Guards (`EVENTS.md` Integration)
*   Renderers MUST implement event guards to prevent network noise.
*   User interactions (taps, text changes, drags) MUST NEVER emit outbound event opcodes (`0xE0`–`0xEF`) unless the target node explicitly contains a bound callback property (`PROP_ACTION_ID` `0x0020` or `PROP_BINDING_ID` `0x0022`).

31: ## Event model
32: 
33: Events flow **host → guest**. The renderer is the producer; the app/engine is
34: the consumer. Both directions of the protocol are binary and share the same
35: 16-byte opcode format; events are `EVENT`-category (0x03) opcodes.
36: 
37: ### Who emits what
38: 
39: - The **renderer** observes native input (a GTK controller, a DOM listener) and
40:   writes raw `EVENT` opcodes. It never interprets them into high-level actions.
41: - The **app** drains the events, composes gestures/handlers, and updates its
42:   bound `State` signals (which in turn re-emit `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`
43:   deltas).
44: - The renderer reports an event for a node **only if that node declared it**
45:   wants it, via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (`0x2005`, a u32
46:   bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type). This makes **any element**
47:   (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit events, not just controls.
48: 
49: ### Target resolution
50: 
51: The renderer resolves `targetId` from its own rendered-output tree (its
52: `id → native element` map): the event's position is hit-tested against that
53: tree to find the deepest node with the matching listener bit. If no listener is
54: declared, the event is not reported.

58: | Path | Mechanism |

61: | Network batch (SSR → browser) | Host → guest batches are the planned `0x0001` direction flag of the `PLPL` batch format; not yet implemented (see OPCODE.md Transport). |

### Who emits what

- The **renderer** observes native input (a GTK controller, a DOM listener) and
  writes raw `EVENT` opcodes. It never interprets them into high-level actions.
- The **app** drains the events, composes gestures/handlers, and updates its

  deltas).
- The renderer reports an event for a node **only if that node declared it**
  wants it, via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (`0x2005`, a u32
  bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type). This makes **any element**
  (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit events, not just controls.

### Transport-aware event guards (MUST)

Renderers **MUST** implement event guards to prevent network noise. A user
interaction — tap, text change, drag, value edit — **MUST NEVER** produce an
outbound event opcode unless the target node explicitly declared intent in **at
least one** of these ways:

1. it set the matching `EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) bits, **or**
2. it is a **value-bearing control** reporting by component type (`SLIDER`,
   `TOGGLE`, `PICKER`, `MENU`, `DATE_PICKER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, …), **or**
3. it carries a bound callback property — `ACTION_ID` (0x2016) or `BINDING_ID`
   (0x2017) — that identifies where the interaction must be routed.

Interactions that match none of these are **dropped at the renderer**; they are
never serialized to the event ring or a network batch. This is the wire-level
guard: a `Button` tap with no `ACTION_ID`, no `BINDING_ID`, and no
`EVENT_LISTENERS` produces no events.

1: # Pathland Primitive Views
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** August 28, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Introduction
10: 
11: This document is the **semantic catalog of primitive nodes** the Pathland
12: protocol supports, organized by the three structural categories that drive
13: rendering. The **server** (the application/engine) dictates *what* the UI is —
14: structure, content, and intent. The **client platform renderer** measures
15: layout geometry, handles font/image assets, and maps each node onto that
16: platform's native elements, delegating interaction to native OS controls
17: wherever possible.
18: 
19: Every primitive maps to a protocol component type (`TREE::CREATE_NODE`), the
20: modifiers that shape it ([MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md)), and the core events it
21: can produce ([EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)). This file is **implementation-ready**: a
22: renderer (GTK, HTML/SSR, Angular/ngui, or a new backend) can be written from
23: these tables alone. The wire encoding rules live in
24: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md); this file does not repeat them.
25: 
26: ### Structural categories
27: 
28: The protocol splits all supported nodes into three structural categories (the
29: component ID ranges are definitive — see [Definitive Opcode
30: Mapping Range](#definitive-opcode-mapping-range)):
31: 
32: | Range | Category | Behavior |
33: |-------|----------|----------|
34: | `0x01`–`0x0F` | **Primitive Drawing Nodes** | Low-level, non-decomposable building blocks (`Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`). The server dictates exact visual content and structural properties. The client measures layout geometry, handles font/image assets, and paints native elements. They hold **no independent interaction state machines**. |
35: | `0x10`–`0x1F` | **Layout & Container Primitives** | Structural arrangement (`VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, lazy grids/stacks). They arrange children and own scroll/virtualization; they carry no interaction semantics beyond scrolling. |
36: | `0x20`–`0x2F` | **Semantic Control Nodes** | High-order interaction and input controls (`Button`, `TextField`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `Picker`, `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`, `Menu`). They encapsulate intent, two-way bindings (`BINDING_ID`), accessibility traits, and local interaction physics (e.g. 120 FPS client-side thumb dragging). |
37: 
38: ### Relationship to other specs
39: 
40: | File | Role |
41: |------|------|
42: | [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md) | Wire format: categories, commands, 16-byte opcode layout, ring/arena, value types |
43: | **PRIMITIVES.md** (this file) | Which **views/nodes** exist and their protocol IDs |
44: | [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md) | Which **modifiers** (protocol properties) exist and how they encode |
45: | [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) | Which **core events** (raw inputs) exist and how they encode |
46: | [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) | Golden byte vectors |
47: 
48: ### Status legend
49: 
50: - **✅ Implemented** — the component type and/or property exists in
51:   `pathland_core::constants` and is exercised by the Rust engine, the Java DSL,
52:   or a renderer today.
53: - **🚧 Draft** — the protocol ID is **allocated** in this document (spec-first,
54:   per the "modify the spec first" rule) but the primitive is not implemented
55:   anywhere yet. IDs are reserved and MUST NOT be reused; implementers may start
56:   on them.
57: 
58: > **Enum-valued properties** (marked `ENUM` in the tables below) are carried on
59: > the wire with the `F32` value type, holding the numeric enum code as an f32
60: > bit pattern (see [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#value-types)). The codes are listed
61: > in [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#appendix-enumerated-values).
62: 
63: ### Non-negotiables (recap)
64: 
65: - Views are **declarative structure + constraint properties**, never positions.
66:   The engine emits `WHAT` (VStack, HStack, Text, …), never `WHERE`.
67: - Renderers are **stateless**: they map the opcode stream onto native elements
68:   and lay those elements out with their native layout engine. A renderer MAY
69:   retain its rendered-output tree for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing —

Spec-only restructure complete. Summary of what changed:

**`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (rewritten, 623 lines) — new Introduction + **Architectural Rules**: §1 Core Structural Classification (Primitive Drawing `0x01–0x0F` / Layout & Container `0x10–0x1F` / Semantic Control `0x20–0x2F`), §2 Dual-Mode Rendering (Native Token Mode → native OS control; Composite Override Mode → custom body + native gesture/focus wrapping; Leaf Property Fallbacks), §3 Transport-Aware Event Guards. Then the definitive A/B/C mapping tables (with `COMMENT`→`0x7F` and the composite-view note for List/NavStack/NavSplit/Label), per-group primitive sections with renderer responsibilities, **tabular property specs for Button (0x20), Toggle (0x24), Slider (0x25)**, and the full **Menu (0x29) structural spec** (native-token leaf trigger, composite custom-trigger, trigger + action-item child rules, native menu-item mapping).

**`spec/OPCODE.md`** — semantic properties updated (`SELECTED` → `TOGGLE`; new drafts `ACTION_ID` 0x2016, `BINDING_ID` 0x2017, `TOGGLE_STYLE` 0x2018); `SWITCH`/`CHECKBOX` paragraph replaced with the `TOGGLE` + `TOGGLE_STYLE` token model; `SLIDER` → 0x25; ROLE value 8 → `Toggle`; event-guard link.

**`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** — `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`TOGGLE_STYLE` added to the catalog + default value types; enum appendix gains `TOGGLE_STYLE` (Switch=0, Checkbox=1, Button=2).

**`spec/EVENTS.md`** — new **Transport-aware event guards (MUST)** section; `VALUE_CHANGED` semantics → `TOGGLE` (dropped `SWITCH`/`CHECKBOX`, `TAB_VIEW`), gated by `BINDING_ID`.

**`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** — vectors 1 & 13 `VSTACK` 0x0002 → **0x0010**. ⚠️ `cargo test` will fail until the deferred code pass renumbers `constants.rs`.

**`AGENTS.md` / `README.md`** — Quick Reference component/property tables renumbered to the new ranges + new properties; README points at the three catalogs.

The earlier uncommitted code changes (value_type / INSERT_APPEND cleanups) are untouched, as requested. Nothing committed.
